newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed weaker, after opening up, with weaker bunds and investor disinterest driving the market down, dealers said.
Nervousness lingered ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting starting later on Tuesday, despite most expectations that U.S. rates will be left unchanged this time round.
Institutional investors mostly hung back, although some traders said the higher yields encouraged a few back in.
"There wasn't much customer-driven business, although it was better than in the last couple of days," one trader said.

Many agreed that yields would have to rise much further before end investors decided to return en masse, but with liquidity still tight, traders argued there was also little scope for sharp price falls.
Customer business that did take place included some switching from Jan 2006s to the new Feb 2007s and from old five year paper, Sept 2001s, to 2002s.
"There's a general bit of reshuffling, but not a whole lot more," one trader said.
